Public evidence does not establish where specific RF/hardware lab facilities are located, so Reading should be treated as a confirmed R&D/engineering presence rather than a verified hardware-lab location. Current UK public vacancies found recently are more software/security/operations oriented than hardware/RF. No current independent-contractor engagement model has been verified. Because this is a prior-employer relationship, outreach should be personal and context-aware rather than a generic application. Prior direct familiarity with Etherstack's mission-critical-radio engineering context materially changes the approach: establish what the Reading/UK team currently owns, whether hands-on hardware/RF/test work is local, and whether a project/contract engagement could solve a current need. companies.name: UK Hands-on Electronics Contract Market — identifiable employers
companies.status: Live contractor intelligence — direct vs inferred employer attribution
companies.text: Why interesting Consolidated market entry for current UK hands-on electronics/RF contracts where the underlying engineering company is either directly identifiable or can be narrowed with useful confidence. This is intentionally kept as one combined Companies record to avoid clutter while preserving the distinction between verified employer identity and attribution by technical/location fingerprint. The strongest current patterns are practical rather than purely design-office work: RF/product validation, automated production test, prototype/rework, component-level diagnosis, manufacturing support, obsolescence, existing-product problem solving, lab verification and hardware/software integration. Attribution grades used here: DIRECT / VERIFIED — employer explicitly named by first-party material, an employer-controlled contingent portal, or the contract advert itself. HIGH-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE — anonymous client, but several unusually specific indicators independently align with one company. Useful for outreach, but not a fact. POSSIBLE / INVESTIGATIVE LEAD — some indicators align, but are not unique enough to attach the vacancy to that company as fact. Working-style fit This group is strongly aligned with hands-on integration/problem-resolution work rather than narrow clean-sheet ownership alone. The highest-fit signals are roles that combine bench measurement with production or lifecycle responsibility: automated test, RF validation, prototype bring-up, rework, fault isolation, manufacturing engineering, component substitution/obsolescence, calibration and existing-product correction. Current strongest technical/work-style matches: 1. Cambridge RF contractor — existing radio product range, 400–900 MHz PMR, TX/RX, VCO, validation, obsolescence, manufacturing support and EMC debug. 2. Cambridge Test Equipment Engineer — automated production test systems, lifecycle support, manufacturing fault-finding and RF-capable lab instrumentation. 3. Warwickshire Electronic Design Engineer — explicit soldering, rework, prototyping and testing alongside Altium/customer work. 4. Andover Electronics Engineer — practical laboratory verification of safety-critical analogue/digital hardware, with DFMEA, traceability, motor control, sensors and microcontrollers. 5. MBDA Bolton Development and Production Test Engineer — direct contingent route, electronics production/test and diagnostic work. 6. Oxford Quantum Circuits Reading FPGA/hardware activity — direct company identity; hands-on RF SoC/high-speed interface and laboratory integration relevance, though FPGA-heavy. Contractor evidence ### MBDA UK — Bolton Attribution: DIRECT / VERIFIED. MBDA's own Guidant Global contingent-worker site currently lists Development and Production Test Engineer - Electronic/Electrical at Bolton and explicitly identifies Bolton as an MBDA manufacturing site. Employer identity therefore does not depend on inference. Direct indicators: employer-controlled MBDA contingent-worker portal Bolton manufacturing site current temporary vacancy development/production electronics test contingent pay structure published Safe claim: MBDA Bolton is currently using contingent electronics/test engineers. ### Oxford Quantum Circuits — Reading Attribution: DIRECT company identity. Current public hiring clearly identifies Oxford Quantum Circuits in Reading for FPGA engineering, including senior FPGA hiring. Earlier contract-market evidence identified an OQC contract/interim FPGA role with hands-on RF SoC, high-speed ADC/DAC, hardware/software integration and laboratory debugging. Treat company identity as direct when the advert itself names OQC; verify the exact contract status again before representing a specific opening as still live. Direct indicators: OQC explicitly named in Reading FPGA vacancies Reading engineering location FPGA/hardware integration ownership Fit caveat: more FPGA-centric than the preferred broad electronics/RF troubleshooting profile. ### Cambridge RF Contractor — probable Sepura Attribution: HIGH-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE — NOT VERIFIED. Direct advert indicators: Cambridge £70/hour six months Outside IR35 minimum four days onsite senior RF contractor existing product range rather than isolated research discrete RF design and validation FGen/VCO and TX/RX circuits 400–900 MHz PMR explicitly relevant integrated products rather than isolated RF modules RF component availability and obsolescence manufacturing-engineering interaction LTE/module/chipset integration desirable EMC debug desirable practical, delivery-focused problem solving Inference indicators toward Sepura: Cambridge/Waterbeach location mission-critical PMR/TETRA product domain several-hundred-MHz integrated radio hardware mature product range with component/obsolescence pressure narrowband mission-critical radio plus LTE/4G/5G transition development engineering combined with manufacturing/product support The combination is unusually specific and maps strongly to Sepura, but the recruiter does not name the client. Internal wording should remain: anonymous Cambridge RF contract; high-confidence inference that the client is Sepura . Do not state that Sepura is advertising the £70/hour contract unless the recruiter or Sepura confirms the client. ### Cambridge Test Equipment Engineer — possible Sepura Attribution: MEDIUM/HIGH INFERENCE — weaker than the RF vacancy. Direct advert indicators: Cambridge Outside IR35 automated production test systems complex electronic products validation and lifecycle support of test equipment manufacturing support/fault-finding multidisciplinary engineering environment Sepura is a plausible candidate because complete professional-radio manufacturing requires exactly this sort of automated production-test capability, and the timing/location overlaps the RF requirement. However, this fingerprint is less unique: many Cambridge electronics, instrumentation and medical-device companies operate comparable test systems. Keep this vacancy separate from the Sepura RF attribution unless another indicator links them. ### Motorola Solutions / Silent Sentinel — Ware Attribution: STRONG INVESTIGATIVE LEAD / HIGH-CONFIDENCE LOCATION-DOMAIN MATCH. Direct company indicators establish Motorola Solutions/Silent Sentinel as an active physical product-engineering presence in Ware, with rugged surveillance hardware and local engineering/support activity. Anonymous Ware contract indicators previously found: prototype hardware PCB modification/rework fine soldering design changes laboratory testing practical troubleshooting These align well with Silent Sentinel's Ware hardware operation, but the contract advert itself did not name Motorola. Safe wording: Motorola/Silent Sentinel is a strong candidate for the Ware electronics contract ; not the Ware contract is Motorola . ### Andover Electronics Engineer — possible Stannah Attribution: POSSIBLE / INVESTIGATIVE LEAD. Direct advert indicators from Owen Daniels: Andover three months Outside IR35 £52–£58/hour safety-critical electronics analogue/digital hardware and PCBs DFMEA requirements traceability practical laboratory verification motor control/sensors/microcontrollers/communications relevance DC electrical systems Stannah is an obvious Andover engineering company to investigate because its products combine safety-critical electromechanical systems, motor control, sensors and electronics. These characteristics are not unique enough to prove attribution. Do not create a Stannah contractor fact from this vacancy without another direct indicator. ### Warwick / Stratford-upon-Avon Electronic Design Engineer Attribution: POSSIBLE / INVESTIGATIVE LEAD. Direct advert indicators: £45–£55/hour Outside IR35 3–6 months Warwickshire / short-notice access to Stratford-upon-Avon Altium schematic/PCB work analogue/digital electronics explicit prototyping, soldering, rework and testing customer and supplier interaction This looks more like a small customer-facing product-development/engineering consultancy than a large OEM. Ex Dynamics or another Stratford-area engineering consultancy is a plausible lead, but there is not enough unique evidence to attach the vacancy to Ex Dynamics as fact. ### Reading Electronics Engineer Attribution: UNRESOLVED. The contract is technically interesting because it combines existing and new products, prototype testing, validation/calibration, production support, contract-manufacturer interaction, obsolescence, DFM, troubleshooting and spectrum-analyser use. PFO Instruments / PE Fiberoptics was identified as one candidate, but the indicators are not sufficiently unique. Keep the vacancy anonymous until stronger evidence appears. Current route Use attribution confidence to decide how to approach each opportunity: DIRECT / VERIFIED: approach the named engineering company and/or its contingent supplier directly. MBDA is the cleanest current example. HIGH-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE: use the suspected employer to guide targeted outreach while keeping the wording conditional. For the Cambridge RF requirement, a direct Sepura approach is justified because the technical fingerprint is unusually strong, but do not claim recruiter confirmation. POSSIBLE / INVESTIGATIVE: first seek one more identifying signal — recruiter disclosure, matching employer-controlled vacancy, unique job/reference wording, simultaneous first-party hiring, direct contact or a distinctive product/location fingerprint. Priority for active pursuit: 1. Cambridge RF contract / probable Sepura 2. Cambridge Test Equipment Engineer 3. MBDA Bolton contingent electronics/test 4. Warwickshire hands-on electronics contract 5. Andover safety-critical electronics contract 6. Motorola/Silent Sentinel Ware lead 7. OQC Reading where the role balance is sufficiently hardware/integration-heavy 8. Reading unresolved electronics contract Caveats High-confidence inference is useful for deciding who to contact; it must not silently become a verified employer fact. Preserve two fields conceptually for anonymous contracts: observed vacancy and candidate employer attribution . A location match alone is not sufficient for attribution. Similar role requirements across safety-critical electronics, automated test and embedded hardware can occur at many companies. Current openings can close quickly; re-verify live status before outreach. Contractor route and employer fit remain separate judgements. A verified contractor mechanism does not imply every project is a strong technical/cultural match. Existing individually curated company records such as Sepura, Etherstack, Cambridge Consultants, Blighter and Rohill remain unchanged; this entry is supplemental market intelligence, not a replacement. Evidence https://mbda.guidantglobal.com/sites https://www.contractoruk.com/job/420969-rf_contractor https://www.contractoruk.com/job/425036-test_equipment_engineer https://www.contractoruk.com/job/433175-electronics_engineer https://www.owendaniels.co.uk/job/electronics-engineer-9 https://uk.linkedin.com/jobs/fpga-jobs https://www.motorolasolutions.com/ https://sepura.com/ https://www.stannah.com/ Private notes Operational rule for future contractor sweeps: never collapse recruiter-anonymous demand into a named employer without retaining the evidence grade. Store/describe employer_attribution , confidence , direct_indicators and inference_indicators separately. Promote to verified only when direct confirmation appears: recruiter disclosure, identical employer-controlled vacancy, employer contingent portal, unique reference number, explicit client statement, or direct contact. This combined entry is deliberately broad to keep #220 and the Companies page usable. Promote an individual company to its own dossier only when there is a verified live route, direct relationship, unusually strong fit, or enough new evidence to justify ongoing curation. companies.name: UK hardware-facing embedded and test contracts — low-level MCU / bring-up / instrumentation lane
companies.status: Live contractor intelligence — explicit hardware-facing embedded/test search lane
companies.text: Why interesting A distinct contractor lane exists between pure electronics/RF work and conventional full-stack embedded software: firmware used to control, interrogate, validate and recover real hardware. The strongest fit is low-level MCU/peripheral work, board bring-up, device-facing communications, test firmware, fixtures, instrumentation and hardware/firmware fault isolation rather than Linux application stacks or broad software-platform ownership. Working-style fit Prioritise roles where the engineer can move freely between schematic/datasheet, firmware, bench measurement and the physical product. Strong signals include PIC/STM32/NXP/Microchip-class MCU work, register-level peripheral control, UART/I2C/SPI/CAN, bare-metal or modest RTOS code, JTAG/SWD, oscilloscopes/logic analysers, board bring-up, automated test, production support and difficult interface/debug problems. Treat Linux kernel/BSP/device-driver ownership as a materially different lane unless the role is unusually hardware-led. The current search also reinforces an important market-language point: PIC-class work is often hidden behind generic terms such as embedded C , low-level drivers , board bring-up , firmware maintenance , sustaining , test equipment , production support , UART/SPI/I2C and hardware/firmware integration . Searching for the work pattern is likely to outperform searching specifically for PIC contractor . Contractor evidence ### Cambridge Test Development Engineer — SoCode recruiter / client not disclosed Current outside-IR35 Cambridge contract, approximately £45–£55/hour and initially around eight months. The advertised work is system-level test development grounded in electronics: test fixtures, automated test systems, troubleshooting and work across software/mechanical boundaries. Employer identity is not established from the advert; SoCode is the recruiter, not the canonical employer. ### Cambridge Test Equipment Engineer — Platform Recruitment / client not disclosed Current outside-IR35 contract centred on automated production test equipment, electronic measurement, instrument communications, manufacturing support, root-cause investigation and RF-capable lab equipment including spectrum/network analysis. Strong practical fit. Platform Recruitment is an intermediary and must not be canonicalised as the engineering employer from this evidence alone. ### Cambridge Contract Electronics Engineer — Redline Group / client not disclosed Current Cambridge contract advertised at approximately £40–£50/hour, outside IR35, 3–6 months, for an urgent beta-phase product. Work includes electronics/PCB activity, testing, commissioning, microcontrollers and sensors. Good cross-domain fit if the actual balance is bring-up/integration/debug rather than primarily clean-sheet Altium ownership. Redline is the recruiter, not the end employer. ### Berkshire Embedded Firmware Engineer — IC Resources recruiter / client not disclosed Current six-month contract advertised around £55–£65/hour. The technical pattern is a strong fit: Embedded C, hands-on board bring-up, SPI/I2C/UART/CAN, oscilloscopes/logic analysers, datasheet-led debugging and hardware/software fault isolation. MCU vendor is not the important point here; the role is explicitly close to the board and physical interfaces. IC Resources is the recruiter, so the end employer remains anonymous. ### Milton Keynes Electronics / Embedded C contract — Zenovo recruiter / client not disclosed Current six-month outside-IR35 contract advertised around £54/hour. Particularly strong fit because the role combines electronics with low-level driver development for SPI/I2C/UART/ADC/DAC, hardware/firmware integration, debugging and bring-up. This is close to the target boundary role rather than a conventional software-only embedded position. Zenovo is an intermediary; do not canonicalise it as the engineering end employer from this vacancy. ### Reading Firmware Engineer — Vantage Consulting recruiter / client not disclosed Current outside-IR35 contract advertised around £50–£60/hour. Relevant signals include MCU firmware, SPI/I2C/UART, JTAG, oscilloscopes and system integration. Fit is weaker than Berkshire/Milton Keynes because the role also carries FPGA/Verilog and defence-domain expectations, but it remains useful evidence that practical MCU/peripheral work exists in the contract market. Vantage Consulting is the recruiter and the end employer is not established. ### Leicester low-level embedded contract — client not disclosed Current outside-IR35 embedded contract in the £45–£60/hour range with low-level C/Python, bare-metal/RTOS, low-level drivers and hardware interfaces. Technically credible stretch because the software remains close to hardware; safety-critical/DO-178C expectations are the main fit caveat. Do not infer the employer without stronger evidence. ### Pragmatic Design Solutions — Coventry embedded contract route A contractor advert names Pragmatic Design Solutions directly and asks for microcontroller work across STM32/NXP/Microchip/AVR-class devices, bare-metal/RTOS, I2C/SPI/UART/CAN, schematics/datasheets, JTAG/SWD, oscilloscopes and logic analysers, with an outside-IR35 day-rate option. This is the clearest named engineering-services employer in the current embedded search and is strongly aligned with hardware-facing low-level work. The same vacancy has been reposted on Contract Spy on a roughly weekly cadence, so repeated listings should be treated as refreshes of one standing/evergreen requirement rather than evidence of multiple simultaneous vacancies. PDSL itself is a genuine engineering-services company; however, the ultimate product/end client behind any particular assignment may still be another organisation. The advert's stated 0–3 years experience is unusual relative to the contractor scope and reduces confidence that this is an urgent senior-contractor requirement. Current route Search and outreach should deliberately include low-level firmware , hardware bring-up , device drivers , peripheral integration , embedded test , test development , test equipment , hardware/firmware integration , electronics debug , production test , sustaining , firmware maintenance , obsolescence , sensor interface and MCU rather than relying on the generic embedded software engineer title. Prioritise urgent project/problem contracts where practical electronics literacy and rapid fault isolation can outweigh a conventional full embedded-Linux stack. Current priority within this lane: 1. Berkshire embedded firmware / bring-up — strong fit, anonymous client. 2. Milton Keynes electronics + low-level drivers — very strong fit, anonymous client. 3. Cambridge test development / test equipment — strong cross-domain fit, anonymous clients. 4. Pragmatic Design Solutions — named engineering-services route, technically strong but likely evergreen/junior-biased requirement. 5. Reading firmware — credible stretch due FPGA/defence content. 6. Leicester low-level embedded — credible stretch due safety-critical process depth. Caveats Do not claim embedded-Linux/full-stack capability from this evidence; Linux kernel/BSP-heavy roles remain a separate and weaker-fit category. Recruiters named above are evidence sources/intermediaries, not necessarily target employers. Several client identities remain undisclosed and should stay anonymous until independently attributable. Safety-critical roles may impose process/certification depth beyond the preferred pragmatic integration niche. Repeated job-board postings can represent one evergreen vacancy rather than multiple openings. Live contract adverts can expire quickly; preserve historical evidence but keep current-status language dated. companies.name: UK Land Mobile Radio Hardware — TETRA / P25 target group
companies.text: Why interesting Consolidated target group for UK organisations with meaningful involvement in professional / mission-critical land-mobile-radio hardware, particularly TETRA and P25. This entry deliberately groups secondary targets to avoid creating a separate Companies dossier for every organisation. ### Simoco Wireless Solutions — Derby Strongest additional UK hardware target in this group. Simoco supplies P25 portable and mobile radios, base stations, repeaters and deployable radio infrastructure. Relevant areas include radio-system integration, RF/infrastructure validation, commissioning, fault diagnosis, product support and performance testing. Website: https://simoco.com/ ### EARS plc — UK Smaller practical radio-engineering organisation rather than a radio OEM. Particularly interesting because its work includes systems engineering, bench work, radio configuration, commissioning, repair, installation and maintenance across professional-radio platforms including Tait, Simoco and Motorola equipment. Potentially attractive for broad hands-on problem ownership. Website: https://earsplc.com/ ### Tait Communications UK Major P25 / DMR professional-radio manufacturer with genuine portable, mobile and base-station/repeater hardware. Core product development is substantially centred outside the UK, particularly New Zealand, so the UK opportunity should be investigated for systems, integration, validation, support and project engineering rather than assuming local RF product design. Website: https://www.taitcommunications.com/ ### Motorola Solutions / Airwave UK Large incumbent mission-critical communications organisation with extensive TETRA infrastructure, subscriber hardware and the Airwave network ecosystem. Technically relevant but substantially more corporate than the preferred small/pragmatic-company profile. Worth monitoring for specialist hardware, integration, validation, obsolescence and product-support opportunities. Website: https://www.motorolasolutions.com/ Working-style fit The common attraction is practical land-mobile-radio engineering rather than protocol/software work alone: radio hardware, RF infrastructure, validation, test, commissioning, integration, production support, fault isolation and maintenance of deployed products. Fit varies substantially by organisation: Simoco is the strongest direct product/infrastructure target in this group. EARS may offer the broadest practical bench/system ownership despite not being an OEM. Tait has strong hardware relevance but UK ownership of RF design needs verification. Motorola/Airwave has deep domain relevance but a much larger and more formal organisation. Contractor evidence No single contractor model applies across this group and no current independent-contractor route is asserted here. Treat contractor compatibility separately for each organisation: Simoco: investigate direct project/contract engineering routes. EARS: small engineering-services structure makes project-based engagement worth asking about, but not verified. Tait UK: contractor route unverified. Motorola Solutions/Airwave: contractors are plausible in the wider programme ecosystem, but a suitable current hardware/RF engagement has not been verified. Current route Use this as a research/outreach queue rather than a single application target. Priority: 1. Simoco — investigate UK engineering ownership and project/contract needs. 2. EARS — investigate bench, systems, commissioning and problem-resolution work. 3. Tait UK — establish what engineering responsibility exists locally. 4. Motorola Solutions/Airwave — monitor selectively for practical RF/hardware/integration work. Position around hands-on professional-radio engineering: RF/product validation, test automation, integration, fault isolation, commissioning, production support, obsolescence/component substitution and solving difficult existing-product problems. Caveats This is intentionally a consolidated sector entry rather than one legal entity. Do not infer P25 and TETRA protocol equivalence; they are separate standards within the same mission-critical LMR domain. Presence of a company's hardware in the UK does not prove that RF hardware development occurs in the UK. Contractor engagement must be verified individually. Existing individually curated companies such as Sepura and Etherstack remain separate and should not be replaced by this entry. Evidence https://simoco.com/solutions/p25/ https://simoco.com/ https://earsplc.com/ https://earsplc.com/jobs/ https://www.taitcommunications.com/products/p25-radio https://www.motorolasolutions.com/en_xu/whats-new/tetra Private notes Consolidated secondary UK LMR-hardware target list to prevent Companies-page clutter. Sepura and Etherstack already justify their own dossiers and remain separate. Promote one of these organisations to an individual dossier only if stronger evidence emerges: a live role, credible contractor route, direct contact, unusually strong technical fit or active outreach. companies.text: Why interesting Fresh RF-focused result set with an explicit exclusion rule: do not pursue military/defence programmes, weapons, missiles, tactical systems, military radar, or roles whose programme requires defence/security clearance. The aim is to retain the same hands-on bring-up/debug/test/validation profile while steering toward commercial wireless, semiconductor, medical technology and civilian telecoms. Current strongest non-military signals: ### Livingston — Senior Analogue/RF Design Engineer — medical robotics Direct advert facts: Posted 21 August 2026. £60–£65/hour. Outside IR35. Initial 14-week contract with stated likelihood of extension across a wider 12–18 month programme. Explicit Healthcare sector. Advanced medical electronics for a next-generation robotic surgical system. Analogue circuit design plus RF/wireless integration. Hardware integration, verification, validation and prototype/product-development support. Engineering investigations and technical problem solving. Interpretation: strongest currently verified non-military RF/electronics contract because the application domain is explicitly medical rather than defence-adjacent. ### Cambridgeshire — RF / Electronics Lab Contractor — wireless/semiconductor Direct advert facts: Current WA Consultants vacancy; recruiter page lists it among recent vacancies and says posted within the last few days. Contract starts ASAP and runs initially to end of year. Onsite Cambridgeshire. Inside IR35; rate flexible, secondary listings show approximately £550/day. Leading-edge wireless / semiconductor client. Pre-silicon and post-silicon validation/verification. Manage RF laboratory and test equipment. Build RF test stands. PCB rework down to 0402 SMD. PCB design/debug. Measurement automation with LabVIEW. Cadence support and IC product-engineering exposure. Interpretation: exceptional work-style fit for practical RF lab ownership, test infrastructure, PCB rework/debug and silicon/product validation. Client is anonymous but the advert itself identifies the sector as wireless/semiconductor with no defence requirement stated. ### Cambridge/Cambourne — commercial wireless systems architecture Direct advert facts: X4 Technology contract for an innovative company developing market-leading wireless products. £60–£80/hour range shown in recruiter material. Outside IR35, QDOS assessed. Six-month contract. Majority remote with Cambridge collaboration. Small specialised engineering team. Whole-system ownership across electronics, digital systems, RF, testing, integration and end application. Interpretation: broader than a pure RF bench role but potentially strong because it values cross-domain ownership rather than narrow specialism. No defence programme is stated in the advert reviewed. ### Cambridge — Principal RF Systems Engineer / advanced wireless test & measurement Direct advert facts: Commercial advanced wireless test and measurement positioning. Contract / Outside IR35 in recruiter material. High rate, majority remote/hybrid Cambridge. RF and mixed-signal architecture. Prototype bring-up, debugging and system-level validation. Calibration and RF characterisation. 2.4 GHz and 5–7 GHz hardware. VNAs, spectrum analysers, signal generators and oscilloscopes. High-frequency PCB debugging. FPGA/DSP/embedded/software interaction. Status caveat: public mirrors disagree on whether this exact vacancy remains active, so treat it as a strong recent lead and confirm with X4 before investing time. ### UK mobile-network deployment — Nokia BTS Installation & Commissioning Direct advert facts: Civil telecommunications infrastructure. Outside IR35. London / Manchester with nationwide travel. Current August/September deployment demand. Nokia BTS baseband, RRHs/RFMs, GPS antennas and RF jumpers. Commissioning, integration and acceptance testing. RF/cabling fault identification and customer acceptance. Current adverts identify BT/EE/Nokia-style mobile-network deployment experience as relevant. Interpretation: clearly non-military RF work and genuinely hands-on, but much more field-installation/commissioning oriented than bench/product-development work. Keep as a secondary option rather than a primary technical target. ### Cambridge — cellular RF Test Engineer / probable Forefront RF fingerprint Employer attribution: HIGH-CONFIDENCE INFERENCE, NOT VERIFIED CONTRACT CLIENT. Observed contract wording from SoCode: RF Test Engineer contract, immediate start. Outside IR35. Cambridge area, lab/on-site presence. Early-stage advanced RF hardware. LTE and/or NR TX/RX measurements. S-parameters, gain, noise and linearity. VNAs, spectrum analysers and signal generators. Repeatable RF test setups. Python/MATLAB-style test automation. PCB hands-on work and hardware troubleshooting. Inference indicators toward Forefront RF: Forefront RF is a Cambridge commercial fabless semiconductor company developing RF front-end technology for mobile and connected devices. Forefront's own RF Test Engineer material uses near-identical technical fingerprints: LTE/NR TX/RX characterisation, S-parameters, VNAs/spectrum analysers/signal generators, repeatable automated test setups, PCB handling/soldering and measurement-driven feedback to design/system teams. Forefront's current company material is explicitly commercial cellular/connected-device technology rather than military RF. Caveat: the specific contract advert is older/possibly closed, so do not treat it as a verified live opening. Use the fingerprint to identify Forefront RF as a high-value commercial RF target and ask whether comparable contract/test support is currently needed. Working-style fit Priority by combination of non-military domain and practical engineering ownership: 1. Cambridgeshire wireless/semiconductor RF lab contractor — test stands, PCB rework/debug, lab ownership, validation. 2. Livingston medical robotics analogue/RF — explicit non-military sector, hardware integration and verification, Outside IR35. 3. Cambridge commercial RF Test / Forefront RF-type work — excellent measurement/debug/test-automation fit if contract demand is current. 4. Cambridge/Cambourne wireless systems architecture — broader cross-domain ownership, Outside IR35. 5. Cambridge wireless test-and-measurement systems — prototype bring-up/debug/validation; live status needs confirmation. 6. Nokia BTS commissioning — genuinely hands-on civilian RF but field-heavy. Contractor evidence Livingston: explicit contract, £60–£65/hour, Outside IR35. Cambridgeshire semiconductor RF lab: explicit contract, ASAP, current recruiter vacancy, Inside IR35. Cambourne wireless architecture: explicit six-month contract, Outside IR35. Cambridge wireless test/measurement: recruiter-described contract and Outside IR35; exact live status needs reconfirmation. BTS commissioning: explicit contract, Outside IR35. Forefront RF attribution: company/domain fit strong, but current contract route itself is not verified now. Current route ### Cambridgeshire RF lab Highest immediate practical target. Contact WA Consultants and ask for client sector/product details while explicitly confirming the work is commercial wireless/semiconductor and has no military/defence programme exposure. Position around RF lab ownership, measurement infrastructure, PCB rework/debug, automated test and pre/post-silicon/product validation. ### Livingston medical robotics Apply through Octagon. Emphasise broad analogue/RF integration, prototype/verification work, technical investigations and practical cross-domain engineering. This is the cleanest sector match because healthcare is explicit. ### Forefront RF Treat as direct speculative commercial RF outreach rather than assuming the old contract is still live. Ask whether the Cambridge RF test team has short-term needs around measurement infrastructure, LTE/NR characterisation, test automation, PCB debug or validation backlog. ### Cambourne/X4 wireless systems Ask recruiter to confirm the end client and commercial application before submission. Reject if the programme turns out to require defence clearance or military end-use. ### Nokia BTS deployment Only pursue if field commissioning/travel is acceptable; technically relevant but less aligned with bench/product-problem ownership. Caveats Hard exclusion: military/defence work, weapons, missiles, tactical systems, military radar and explicitly defence-cleared programmes are out of scope. Security clearance is not automatically proof of military work in every UK role, but where the programme is defence/security or weapons-related it should be excluded rather than merely down-ranked. Mission-critical alone is ambiguous: public safety, healthcare and commercial infrastructure can be mission-critical without being military. Check the end application before rejecting or accepting. Anonymous commercial wireless/semiconductor clients still need end-use confirmation before outreach progresses. Forefront RF is a strong employer fingerprint for the Cambridge cellular-test pattern, but the specific older contract is not currently verified live. X4 wireless test/measurement live status is inconsistent across public mirrors; recruiter confirmation required. Do not let high rates or strong technical fit override the military exclusion. Future sweeps should prioritise commercial wireless, semiconductor, telecoms, medical, scientific instrumentation, consumer/industrial RF, civilian satcom only where end-use is clear, and other non-military RF products. The scheduled UK contract watch has also been updated to exclude military/defence programmes rather than surfacing them as normal matches. Last curated: 2026-08-31
